In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods and tools for the systematic and efficient design of complex system products, with a special emphasis on requirements management.
the design of product models that are suitable for supporting the product development process, and with the integration of product models into product information systems.
the development of a new approach for the design of a new approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the development of product and process models should be based on a thorough analysis of the requirements and knowledge structures needed for the product development process, and that the product model should be designed to support the requirements and knowledge structure, not vice versa.
the development of a product model is a complex task that requires careful consideration of the company's specific situation and needs.
the requirement decomposition and propagation process is an important part of the total product development process and should be carefully planned and executed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of requirement structures for product development can be supported with computer implemented information systems.
the requirement driven design process is a promising concept for the future of product development.

the requirement-driven design processes are surprisingly similar in all three companies studied and that there is a great potential for using knowledge structures in the product models to enhance the design process and the design outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a systematic approach to the integration of knowledge structures into product development processes and product models is feasible and can be implemented.
it is possible to design requirement driven processes with integrated knowledge structures that are well suited to complex system products.
the development process can benefit from a well-organized information structure that is based on a systematic decomposition of the requirements and functions.
